# Agentic engineering

## Basic workflow

| Phase | Responsibility |
|:---|:---|
| **1. Explore** | Understand the codebase and conventions. |
| **2. Plan** | Define the steps and success criteria. |
| **3. Code** | Implement, test, and adjust. |
| **4. Commit** | Review, verify, and commit. |

Source: [Claude Academy — The explore → plan → code → commit workflow](https://academy.claude.com/courses/claude-code-101/the-explore-plan-code-commit-workflow)
:::

## Execution environment {.smaller}

The **execution environment** is where the harness reads files, runs tools, and
applies changes. It is a separate choice from the **harness** and the **model**.

| Environment | How it works | Best suited to |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Local** | Works directly in your current checkout | Interactive tasks with immediate feedback |
| **Worktree** | Uses a separate Git checkout and branch on your machine | Isolated or parallel tasks without disturbing your workspace |
| **Cloud** | Runs in a remote, isolated environment and returns a branch or change for review | Delegated tasks that can continue independently |

::: {.fragment}
*Demo: worktree in agents window*
:::

## Instructions {.smaller}

Instructions give the agent **persistent context** it should follow without
repeating it in every prompt.

| File | Purpose |
|:---|:---|
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Repository-wide guidance for GitHub Copilot |
| `AGENTS.md` | Portable agent guidance; nest files to specialize instructions for parts of a repository |
| `CLAUDE.md` | The native project-instructions file for Claude Code |

::: {.fragment}
*Demo: let's look at instructions*
:::

::: footer
Sources: [GitHub Docs — Adding repository custom instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/add-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions) · [VS Code — Custom instructions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions)
:::

## Instructions

Include what the agent cannot reliably infer from the code:

- architecture and important directories,
- build, test, lint, and formatting commands,
- project-specific conventions and constraints,
- what must be verified before a task is complete.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Type `/init` in VS Code Copilot Chat to generate a starting point—then review,
trim, and commit it with the codebase.
:::

::: {.fragment}
*Demo: create instruction using `/init` or `/create-instruction`*
:::

## File-specific instructions {.smaller}

Use `.github/instructions/NAME.instructions.md` when guidance should apply only
to particular files or directories.

**How it works**

- Create one or more files whose names end with `.instructions.md`.
- Set `applyTo` to a glob such as `**/*.py`; separate multiple patterns with
  commas.
- Copilot combines every matching file with the repository-wide instructions.

**When to use it**

- language and framework conventions,
- rules for tests, documentation, or generated code,
- commands specific to one module in a monorepo.

::: footer
Source: [GitHub Docs — Creating path-specific custom instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/add-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions#creating-path-specific-custom-instructions)
:::

## Skills {.smaller}

Skills package **specialized knowledge and repeatable workflows** so agents can
perform particular tasks consistently.

:::: columns
::: {.column width="46%"}
**An open, portable standard**

```text
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md       # instructions
├── scripts/       # optional
├── references/    # optional
└── assets/        # optional
```

Skills can be versioned with the codebase and reused across compatible agent
products.
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
**Progressive disclosure**

1. **Discover** — load only each skill's name and description.
2. **Activate** — read `SKILL.md` when the task matches.
3. **Execute** — load bundled resources only as needed.

This keeps many skills available without filling the agent's context window.
:::
::::

::: {.fragment}
*Demo: let's look at available skills*
:::

::: footer
Source: [Agent Skills — Overview](https://agentskills.io/home)
:::

## Subagents {.smaller}

A **subagent** is an isolated agent with its own context window. It receives a
focused task and returns the relevant result to the main conversation.

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Delegate when the work benefits from:**

- **context isolation** — research without flooding the main conversation,
- **parallelism** — independent tasks can run simultaneously,
- **fresh perspective** — review without the main agent's assumptions.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Keep it with the main agent when:**

- the task is small,
- each step depends tightly on the previous one,
- multiple agents would edit the same file,
- the agents need to coordinate directly.
:::
::::

Delegate a **clear scope**, the **available tools**, and the **expected output**.

::: {.fragment}
*Demo: run subagents*
:::

::: footer
Source: [Claude — How and when to use subagents in Claude Code](https://claude.com/blog/subagents-in-claude-code)
:::

## Hooks {.smaller}

Hooks run **deterministic automation** at specific points in the agent lifecycle.
Unlike instructions, they do not depend on the model remembering to act.

| Lifecycle event | Example use |
|:---|:---|
| `SessionStart` / `UserPromptSubmit` | Initialize resources or add context |
| `PreToolUse` | Inspect or block a risky command before it runs |
| `PostToolUse` | Format changed files, run checks, or record an audit trail |
| `Stop` | Verify the result, clean up, or generate a report |

Workspace hooks live in `.github/hooks/*.json`. VS Code passes event data to the
command as JSON on **stdin**; the command can return JSON on **stdout** to add
context or influence what happens next.

::: footer
Source: [GitHub Docs — GitHub Copilot hooks reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference?tool=vscode&versionId=free-pro-team%40latest&productId=copilot&restPage=concepts%2Cprompting%2Cresponse-customization)
:::
